title: Dilucidationes super methodo elegantissima, qua illustris de la Grange usus est in integranda aequatione differentiali dx/√X = dy/√Y

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Lagrange (Miscellanea Taurinensia, c. 1766–69) obtained an algebraic integral of the separated equation dx/√X = dy/√Y, where X = A+Bx+Cx²+Dx³+Ex⁴ and Y is the same quartic in y. In E506, §4, Euler sets V = √X+√Y and writes the integral as V/(x−y) = √(Δ + D(x+y) + E(x+y)²), with Δ the arbitrary constant. Here D and E are the same coefficients as in the quartic.

This page begins Euler's direct check that this relation really is an integral of the differential equation. He squares it to V²/(x−y)² = Δ + D(x+y) + E(x+y)². Differentiating removes Δ:
2V dV/(x−y)² − 2V²(dx−dy)/(x−y)³ − D(dx+dy) − 2E(x+y)(dx+dy) = 0.

§5 sorts the terms by differential. Holding y fixed gives dV = X′dx/(2√X), so the dx-part is
dx[ V X′/((x−y)²√X) − 2V²/(x−y)³ − D − 2E(x+y) ].
Euler then multiplies through by √X (keeping the 1/√X tacitly in front) and uses V²√X = (X+Y)√X + 2X√Y. This splits the bracket into terms containing √Y and terms containing √X.

The √Y terms are −4X√Y/(x−y)³ + X′√Y/(x−y)². Combined, they give (√Y/(x−y)³)(X′(x−y) − 4X). For the quartic, X′ = B+2Cx+3Dx²+4Ex³, and the x⁴ term cancels in X′(x−y) − 4X. The result is
−4A − B(3x+y) − 2C(x²+xy) − D(x³+3x²y) − 4Ex³y,
which becomes −M on the next page.

The √X terms are (√X/(x−y)³)(X′(x−y) − 2(X+Y) − D(x−y)³ − 2E(x+y)(x−y)³). The next page reduces this to the x↔y mirror image, −N.

The overall plan (§§6–7) is that the dx-part becomes −dx(M√Y+N√X)/((x−y)³√X). The dy-part is the same with x↔y and the sign reversed, so the whole differential is proportional to (M√Y+N√X)(dy/√Y − dx/√X). This shows the relation integrates the equation. The purpose is to verify, and simplify the presentation of, Lagrange's integral of the Euler addition-theorem equation for elliptic differentials.
errors: Printed denominator '(x − y²)' in the term X′√Y/(x−y²) is a misprint for (x−y)²; the combined expression that follows is correct.
The tacit factor 1/√X after multiplying the dx-bracket by √X is not stated on this page; it reappears correctly on the next page (§6).
The last line has an unbalanced parenthesis after (x−y)³ (typographical only).
All algebra checked: the differentiation, X′(x−y) − 4X = −4A − B(3x+y) − 2C(xx+xy) − D(x³+3xxy) − 4Ex³y, and the √X-bracket are correct.

ideas.what: Lagrange's algebraic integral ((√X+√Y)/(x−y))² − D(x+y) − E(x+y)² = const for dx/√X = dy/√Y with X a general quartic
ideas.modern_name: Algebraic form of the addition theorem for elliptic integrals (first kind)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (addition theorem, 1750s); this particular symmetric form to Lagrange (Misc. Taurinensia IV, 1766–69)
ideas.where_published: E506 itself (Acta Acad. Sci. Petropolitanae, published early 1780s); Euler's own earlier forms in E251/E252 and the Institutiones calculi integralis

ideas.what: Direct verification by differentiating to eliminate the arbitrary constant, then separating the terms carrying √X and √Y
ideas.modern_name: Verification of a first integral via the total differential

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine, correct verification computation for a well-known published paper on Lagrange's integral of the elliptic addition equation. Nothing here is new or uncredited.
transcription_corrections: 'Termini autem per √x affecti sunt' should read '√X' (capital X; the print is ambiguous).
'X′√Y/(x−y²)' reproduces a printer's error for X′√Y/(x−y)².
In the polynomial, the print shows exponents as 'x^s' / 'x^⁴'; the correct reading is X = A + Bx + Cxx + Dx³ + Ex⁴.
The final expression should read (√X/(x−y)³)(X′(x−y) − 2(X+Y) − D(x−y)³ − 2E(x+y)(x−y)³), without the stray closing parenthesis.
